verdict.rationale: CoreWeave's pricing page presents on-demand and Spot capacity as the options for when you're 'not looking for long-term capacity commitments,' and Spot docs contrast themselves with 'long-term commitments or reservations.' Both imply a first-party reserved or committed capacity offering exists, but no evidence documents its terms, discount levels, or how a platform engineer locks one in. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of reserved/committed-use plans, published discount terms, a self-serve or API/Terraform way to purchase commitments, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can lock in reserved or committed-use discounts for sustained GPU capacity

citations.quote: Utilize on-demand GPU instances for additional workloads when you're not looking for long-term capacity commitments.
Spot Node Pools provide pay-as-you-go access to high-performance bare-metal compute resources without long-term commitments or reservations.
